'''John Trevor Lewis''' (15 April 1932 – 21 January 2004) was a [[Welsh people|Welsh]] [[mathematical physicist]] who made contributions to areas including quantum measurement, [[Bose–Einstein condensate|Bose–Einstein condensation]] and [[large deviations theory]].<ref name=ims_obit>{{Cite journal
  | last1 = Pule  | first1 = Joseph V.
  | title = John T. Lewis (1932–2004)
  | journal = Bulletin of the Irish Mathematical Society
  | volume = 54
  | pages = 15–24
  | publisher = Irish Mathematical Society
  | year = 2005
 }}</ref> He was a senior professor at the [[Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies]] (DIAS) in [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] from 1972, serving as the director of the School of Theoretical Physics from 1975 until his retirement in 2001.<ref name=dias_obit>[https://www.stp.dias.ie/people/Lewis/obituary.html DIAS obituary for John T. Lewis (1932–2004)]</ref>
He also founded the Communications Networks Research Institute at [[Dublin Institute of Technology]].

==Academic career==
Lewis was born in [[Swansea]], [[Wales]], and was educated at Cardiff High School and then the [[Royal Belfast Academical Institution]].<ref name=dias_obit/> He then studied at [[Queen's University Belfast]], earning BSc in 1952 and PhD in 1955, the latter for a thesis on "Quantal Calculations Relating to Certain Rate Processes" done with [[Alexander Dalgarno]] and [[David Bates (physicist)|David Bates]]. He moved to [[Oxford University|Oxford]] in 1956, initially at Christ Church and later at Brasenose where he acted as Dean.<ref name=mprf_obit>{{Cite journal
  | last1 = Duffy  | first1 = Ken
  | last2 = Pule  | first2 = Joe
  | title = John T. Lewis (1932–2004)
  | journal = Markov Processes and Related Fields
  | volume = 13
  | pages = 3–19
  | publisher = Polymat
  | year = 2007
 }}</ref> In 1969 he spent a year visiting [[Rockefeller University]] and the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref name=itimes_obit>{{cite news
  |title=Theoretical physicist who revolutionised telecoms
  |newspaper=[[The Irish Times]]
  |date=31 January 2004
  |page=12
}}</ref> In 1972, he moved to the [[Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies]] on the retirement of [[John Lighton Synge|John L. Synge]],<ref name=ims_obit/> where he served as director of the School of Theoretical Physics. He was an honorary professor at [[Swansea University|Swansea]], [[Cardiff University|Cardiff]] and [[Trinity College, Dublin]].<ref name=mprf_obit/> He was a member of the [[Royal Irish Academy]] and was its senior vice-president in 1988.<ref name=ims_obit/> He received one of the first honorary doctorates from [[Dublin Institute of Technology]] in 1999.<ref name=dias_obit/>

In 1971, he helped to found the Irish branch of [[Pugwash Conferences on Science and World Affairs|Pugwash]].<ref name=itimes_obit/> With D McQuillan and [[Trevor West|T West]] he drew up the draft constitution of the [[Irish Mathematical Society]] after the DIAS Christmas Symposium in 1975.<ref>[http://www-history.mcs.st-and.ac.uk/Societies/Irish.html The Irish Mathematical Society page on The MacTutor History of Mathematics archive]</ref> From 1985 to 1987 he was president of the [[Irish Federation of University Teachers]].<ref name=mprf_obit/>

Lewis was also a founder of, and chief scientist at, [[Corvil]], a company specialising in measurement and performance of Internet traffic.<ref name=itimes_obit/>
